correctness.rationale: For every integer \(n\ge3\), all positive prices and budgets, injectivity of individual edge weights into a reduced simple-graph Laplacian makes log determinant strictly concave on connected supports and forces a unique unrestricted optimum. Joint permutation of matched vertex labels forces exactly two weight classes. The complete four-block spectral factorization gives the exact weighted tree polynomial; the constrained logarithmic derivative has the stated explicitly signed quadratic numerator. Its sign yields the unique positive radical root below the price threshold, and a boundary optimum above. Differentiation of log tree count plus exact crown resistance identities corroborates the same threshold. The standalone exact-rational grounded determinant and resistance tests and floating-point asymmetric comparisons passed; they are not substitutes for proof.

originality.rationale: Related primary literature establishes general weighted matrix-tree and convex graph-design principles and, much closer, exact matching-containment tree counts and resistances for matching-deleted complete bipartite graphs. Those prior exact coefficient formulas yield the two-orbit unoptimized weighted count but do not state or globally characterize the unique price-budget allocation over all independent edges, its sharp cutoff or the full cost-dependent optimum. General theory plus simple derivations could make the distinction less independent than a wholly new spectral invariant; this is a real residual risk, not proof of uniqueness of discovery.
residual_risks: Ge–Dong Theorem 1.3 encodes every coefficient of the invariant two-weight tree polynomial; calculus plus standard strict-concavity arguments may make the additional price classification straightforward or appear elsewhere.

Earlier Ye–Yan and Shi–Chen graph-resistance papers referenced in Ge–Dong were not independently obtained in full text; they may contain specialized electrical identities but no verified matching-price allocation theorem.
Searches and available primary sources do not prove mathematical uniqueness of publication or priority.

value.rationale: A full closed-form resource-allocation classification for dense bipartite networks with a distinguished perfect matching determines both the unique optimal support and all conductances, including a strict phase transition at a computable resistance-leverage price ratio. The premium for deleting all n matching links tends to zero like 1/n, a nontrivial large-network design effect. This is a natural graph-design optimization, not an arbitrary finite table or isolated parameter computation; it does not rely on any claimed downstream theorem.
